Baggrundspopulationen 2023 (and its subsequent 2024 iteration) refers to the general Danish youth population used as a baseline comparison group in the national ADHD quality monitoring reports. Specifically, it serves as the benchmark for evaluating educational outcomes among young people with ADHD, measured through Indicators 7a and 7b. These indicators track the completion of the Danish primary school leaving exam (*folkeskolens afgangseksamen*) for youth in ADHD assessment and treatment populations, comparing their results against this general background population to highlight structural educational disparities and regional variations.

In the 2023 reporting period, the background population demonstrated an 86% pass rate for the primary school leaving exam [^src1]. Additionally, the proportion of young people in the background population who passed the primary school leaving exam before reaching the age of 17 is 84% [^src2]. These baseline figures are critical for contextualizing the significant educational lag observed among youth with ADHD, underscoring the need for targeted support within the school system and treatment pathways. The data is drawn from the ADHD-Databasen and Danmarks Statistik, forming a core part of the evaluation of national ADHD strategies and quality standards for children and youth.
